correctness.rationale: The patch replaces the two hard-coded install.sh/test.sh checks with an explicit SCRIPT_SYNTAX_GLOBS array covering all five requested locations (*.sh, scripts/*.sh, scripts/checks/*.sh, scripts/setup/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh), runs parser-only bash -n per matched file, and reports each file independently via pass()/fail(). Unmatched patterns are skipped safely because the inner loop uses [[ -f "$file" ]] || continue, so literal glob strings are never passed to bash -n. One point withheld because bundle-only grading provides no executed bash test.sh output to confirm end-to-end runtime behavior.

quality.rationale: Implementation is minimal, readable, and scoped to the single required check file with an explicit glob set and a clear comment block documenting parser-only intent, bats exclusion, and empty-glob handling via the -f guard. Deductions for bash -n stderr suppression (2>/dev/null hides syntax-error detail on failure), unquoted for file in $glob re-expansion (functional for this repo but less defensive than nullglob-plus-quoted-array patterns used elsewhere), and no deduplication layer for the rare case of overlapping pattern matches.

process.rationale: Diff is tightly focused on scripts/checks/055-script-syntax.sh with no unrelated churn (objective process scored 15/15). Bundle contains no plan artifact, doc-sync or no-change decision, verification notes, bash test.sh output, or documented negative-smoke demonstration/explanation required by acceptance criteria, so full plan/verification discipline cannot be confirmed from bundle evidence alone.

reliability.rationale: Objective evidence confirms test wiring (6/6) and bash_n_check_script pass, and the diff integrates with existing pass/fail helpers. Bundle lacks full_test_sh execution evidence (skipped in bundle-only grading), no reported command output, and no negative-smoke test or explanation that a deliberate syntax error is caught and cleared, leaving verification discipline thin despite plausible wiring.

uncertainty_notes: full_test_sh was skipped in objective grading; bundle contains no candidate verification output or negative-smoke evidence for bash test.sh.
Cannot confirm from bundle alone whether expanding coverage would have revealed latent syntax errors elsewhere requiring fixes in the same diff.
